title: shared_two_hub_rank2_receiver
result: For a zero quadratic block on two literal hubs and a rank-two hub-to-rest block B, arbitrary quadratic terms on the rest are allowed and the output density is bounded by e*sqrt(pi)*K^2/det(BB^T)^(1/4).
method: condition on the rest; use scalar projection on the two hubs; average reciprocal distance using the two-dimensional projection density of B times the rest vector
counterexample: Two diffuse orthonormal hub rows sharing the same leaves have four singular values equal to one, no pivot for N>256, and every coordinate crossing block has rank at most two.
next: handle a nonzero two-by-two quadratic hub block
